bio.text: Those who study the old masters and do not introduce some changes [are] as if [closed] in by a fence. If one imitates the models too closely one is often farther removed from them.

bio.text: As a statesman, as a painter, as a calligrapher, as an [archaeologist], and as a writer on art, Tung Ch‘i-ch‘ang enjoyed for fifty years the highest reputation. No ancient picture was genuine till Tung's seal had made it so.

source.author: Arthur Waley
source.title: An Introduction to the Study of Chinese Painting

bio.text: In his art theoretical writings, Dong developed the theory that Chinese painting could be divided into two schools: the "Northern" school, characterized by fine lines and colors, and the "Southern", school noted for its quick calligraphic strokes, as first suggested to him by his friend and older contemporary Mo Shilong.
